paras.en: The team hopes these escape artists will inspire new soft robots that can morph their shape to fit through tiny spaces, says Wenci Xin, a robotics researcher at the National University of Singapore. “This incredible capability could enable robots to overcome environmental limitations and enter spaces that are difficult to reach.”
paras.zh: 新加坡国立大学机器人研究员 Wenci Xin 表示，该团队希望这些逃脱艺术家能够激发新的软机器人的灵感，这些机器人可以改变自己的形状以适应狭小的空间。 “这种令人难以置信的能力可以使机器人克服环境限制并进入难以到达的空间。”

paras.en: Studying how octopuses navigate different types of holes may provide additional clues for robots, Crook says. For instance, the cephalopods may take a different tack for openings that are more like slits or tubes than holes.
paras.zh: 克鲁克说，研究章鱼如何穿过不同类型的洞可能为机器人提供更多线索。例如，头足类动物可能会采用不同的方法来处理更像狭缝或管子而不是孔的开口。

paras.en: Currently, robots built to fit through tiny holes tend to be snake-shaped, but further research on these eight-armed contortionists could unlock other configurations.
paras.zh: 目前，用于穿过小孔的机器人往往是蛇形的，但对这些八臂柔术演员的进一步研究可以解锁其他配置。

articles.title: A Mysterious Asteroid Is Accelerating in Space, And We're Running Out of Explanations
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: They just do what they're told, pushed and tugged by external forces such as gravity or radiation pressure from the Sun.
paras.zh: 他们只是按照指示行事，受到重力或太阳辐射压力等外力的推动和拉扯。

paras.en: KY26 is hooning about like a ne'er-do-well – that is, accelerating in a way that defies expectations for how a well-brought-up asteroid ought to behave.
paras.zh: KY26 的运行速度就像一颗无所事事的小行星——也就是说，它的加速速度违背了人们对一颗良好成长的小行星应有的行为的预期。

paras.en: One proposed explanation for these cosmic monkeyshines is that KY26 is only masquerading as an asteroid – that, in its deep heart of hearts, it's really a 'dark' comet, whose undetectable outgassing is steering it along a different path.
paras.zh: 对这些宇宙猴光的一个拟议解释是，KY26 只是伪装成一颗小行星——在它的内心深处，它实际上是一颗“黑暗”彗星，其不可察觉的放气正在引导它沿着不同的路径前进。

paras.en: But there's now a problem with that explanation.
paras.zh: 但现在这个解释有问题了。

paras.en: According to aerospace engineers Korbin Hansen and Masatoshi Hirabayashi of the Georgia Institute of Technology, the 11-meter (36-foot) space rock is too warm to retain the ice needed to power propulsion.
paras.zh: 佐治亚理工学院的航空航天工程师 Korbin Hansen 和 Masatoshi Hirabayashi 表示，11 米（36 英尺）高的太空岩石温度太高，无法保留推进动力所需的冰。

paras.en: "Our temperature model results indicate that the water outgassing rate on 1998 KY26 would be too high to maintain buried ice, refining the understanding of the asteroid's composition," they write in a paper published in Icarus.
paras.zh: 他们在《伊卡洛斯》发表的一篇论文中写道：“我们的温度模型结果表明，1998 KY26 上的水释气率太高，无法维持埋藏的冰，从而加深了对小行星成分的理解。”

paras.en: The rocks that populate interplanetary space generally fall into two broad categories – asteroids and comets.
paras.zh: 行星际空间中的岩石通常分为两大类——小行星和彗星。

paras.en: Asteroids are mostly lumps of rock, whereas comets contain ice that, as it sublimates into gas and escapes into space, can give the comet a bit of a shove beyond the forces applied by gravity as it orbits the Sun.
paras.zh: 小行星主要是岩石块，而彗星则含有冰，当冰升华成气体并逃逸到太空时，可以给彗星带来一点推力，超越彗星绕太阳运行时重力所施加的力。

paras.en: The image that likely comes to mind when you think of a comet is a shimmering, hazy orb trailed by luminous streamers. But not all comets are built alike.
paras.zh: 当您想到彗星时，您可能想到的图像是一个闪烁着朦胧的球体，拖着发光的流光。但并非所有彗星的构造都是相似的。

paras.en: What we call dark comets are so named because their cometary activity is effectively invisible. They're thought to spew out gases just like an ordinary comet, without producing the spectacular visible tails normally associated with them.
paras.zh: 我们所说的暗彗星之所以如此命名，是因为它们的彗星活动实际上是不可见的。人们认为它们会像普通彗星一样喷出气体，而不会产生通常与它们相关的壮观的可见彗尾。

paras.en: They look just like ordinary asteroids, with a little added acceleration.
paras.zh: 它们看起来就像普通的小行星一样，只是增加了一点加速度。

paras.en: This is what KY26 may look like. The small asteroid rotates once every 5.35 minutes, and its trajectory shows unusual acceleration perpendicular to the plane of its orbit. So naturally, scientists have considered whether it could be one of these dark comets.
paras.zh: 这就是 KY26 的样子。这颗小行星每 5.35 分钟自转一周，其轨迹显示出垂直于轨道平面的异常加速度。因此，科学家自然会考虑它是否可能是这些黑暗彗星之一。

paras.en: One of the defining characteristics of comets is their icy composition, which gives scientists an easy way to check their cometary ID.
paras.zh: 彗星的定义特征之一是它们的冰成分，这为科学家提供了一种简单的方法来检查彗星的ID。

paras.en: All you have to do is take their temperature.
paras.zh: 您所要做的就是测量他们的体温。

paras.en: This is what Hansen and Hirabayashi did. Or rather, they combined what is known about KY26 – its size, its orbit, its reflectivity, and its likely composition – to model temperatures across its surface and deep inside.
paras.zh: 汉森和平林就是这么做的。或者更确切地说，他们结合了 KY26 的已知信息——它的大小、轨道、反射率和可能的成分——来模拟其表面和内部深处的温度。

paras.en: For buried water ice to survive over long periods, temperatures need to remain below around 145 Kelvin (-128 degrees Celsius).
paras.zh: 为了使埋藏的水冰能够长期存在，温度需要保持在 145 开尔文（-128 摄氏度）左右以下。

paras.en: But even the coldest regions of KY26, the researchers found, have an average temperature of at least 212 Kelvin (-61 degrees Celsius) over the course of its orbit around the Sun. That's deathly cold for a human, sure – but far too warm for cometary ice to hang around.
paras.zh: 但研究人员发现，即使是 KY26 最冷的区域，其绕太阳轨道运行的平均温度也至少为 212 开尔文（-61 摄氏度）。当然，这对于人类来说是致命的寒冷，但对于彗星冰来说却太温暖了。

paras.en: At these temperatures, the researchers calculated that even if water ice made up 1 percent of KY26's mass, it would all disappear in just over 2,000 years. And if that ice were responsible for the asteroid's unusual acceleration, it would be gone in just 62 years.
paras.zh: 在这样的温度下，研究人员计算出，即使水冰占KY26质量的1%，它也会在短短2000多年内全部消失。如果这些冰是小行星异常加速的原因，那么它会在短短 62 年内消失。

paras.en: KY26 may be billions of years old – but even so, there is an important caveat. It's not clear how long it has occupied its current orbit. So it's still possible that it has ice – but between this result and an earlier paper tracing KY26 to a potential asteroid belt origin, that possibility is shrinking.
paras.zh: KY26 可能已经有数十亿年的历史了——但即便如此，还是有一个重要的警告。目前尚不清楚它在当前轨道上运行了多久。所以它仍然有可能有冰——但从这一结果和早期的一篇将 KY26 追溯到潜在小行星带起源的论文来看，这种可能性正在缩小。

paras.en: So what could be shoving KY26 off the straight-and-narrow? Well, we can still look at good old peer pressure – if peer pressure means radiation pressure from the Sun. Sunlight exerts a small but potentially powerful enough force that it could be responsible for the asteroid's apparent delinquency.
paras.zh: 那么到底是什么原因让 KY26 偏离了直线轨道呢？好吧，我们仍然可以看看古老的同伴压力——如果同伴压力意味着来自太阳的辐射压力。阳光产生的力量虽小，但可能足够强大，可能是小行星明显犯罪的原因。

paras.en: The great news is that we may find out for certain very soon. The Japanese space agency's Hayabusa2 spacecraft is making its way toward KY26 even as you read these words, with a rendezvous slated for July 2031.
paras.zh: 好消息是我们很快就会得到确定的答案。当你读到这些文字时，日本航天局的隼鸟 2 号航天器正在向 KY26 进发，预计将于 2031 年 7 月会合。

paras.en: Accelerate all you want, KY26. You can't hide forever.
paras.zh: 加速你想要的一切，KY26。你不可能永远隐藏。

paras.en: The research has been published in Icarus.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《伊卡洛斯》杂志上。

articles.title: Humans Are Still Evolving Right Before Our Eyes. Here Are 5 Signs on Our Bodies
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: Our species' evolution is often symbolized as a four-legged chimpanzee slowly morphing into an upright hunter.
paras.zh: 我们物种的进化通常被象征为四足黑猩猩慢慢演变成直立猎人。

paras.en: Today, evidence suggests that humans are still evolving, and it shows in our very physiology: from our skin, to our eyes, to our blood.
paras.zh: 今天，有证据表明人类仍在进化，这体现在我们的生理学中：从我们的皮肤，到我们的眼睛，再到我们的血液。

paras.en: Take, for instance, our gut. It contains one of the strongest documented examples of modern natural selection that scientists have yet found.
paras.zh: 以我们的肠道为例。它包含了科学家迄今为止发现的最有力的现代自然选择的记录例子之一。

paras.en: Roughly 10,000 years ago, humans in some parts of the world began to domesticate cows and other grazers. Then, they learned how to milk these animals.
paras.zh: 大约一万年前，世界某些地区的人类开始驯化牛和其他食草动物。然后，他们学会了如何给这些动物挤奶。

paras.en: But the trouble was, the adult mammalian gut was unprepared for the lactose.
paras.zh: 但问题是，成年哺乳动物的肠道对乳糖没有做好准备。

paras.en: Some of our ancestors, however, had gene variants that meant they could tolerate dairy without getting sick.
paras.zh: 然而，我们的一些祖先有基因变异，这意味着他们可以忍受乳制品而不会生病。

paras.en: Modern gene studies in Europe, East Africa, and the Middle East suggest that over time, variants for lactose tolerance spread through natural selection.
paras.zh: 欧洲、东非和中东的现代基因研究表明，随着时间的推移，乳糖耐受性的变异通过自然选择而传播。

paras.en: Today, that is probably why 30 to 35 percent of the global adult population can tolerate lactose.
paras.zh: 如今，这可能就是全球 30% 至 35% 的成年人能够耐受乳糖的原因。

paras.en: Meanwhile, in the Andes of South America, it is not milk but the potato that has shaped human gut evolution.
paras.zh: 与此同时，在南美洲的安第斯山脉，塑造人类肠道进化的不是牛奶，而是土豆。

paras.en: The Quechua people of highland Indigenous Andean ancestry were some of the first in the world to domesticate the potato.
paras.zh: 拥有安第斯高原原住民血统的盖丘亚人是世界上最早驯化马铃薯的人之一。

paras.en: Earlier this year, researchers found that this population seems better equipped for starch digestion than almost any other on Earth.
paras.zh: 今年早些时候，研究人员发现，这个群体似乎比地球上几乎任何其他群体都更有能力消化淀粉。

paras.en: "Biologists have long suspected that different groups of humans have evolved genetic adaptations in response to their diets," said evolutionary anthropologist Omer Gokcumen of the University at Buffalo.
paras.zh: 布法罗大学的进化人类学家奥马尔·格库门（Omer Gokcumen）说：“生物学家长期以来一直怀疑，不同的人类群体已经进化出了针对其饮食的遗传适应。”

paras.en: "But there are very few cases where the evidence is this strong."
paras.zh: “但证据如此有力的案例很少。”

paras.en: When the ancestors of Indigenous Andeans began growing potatoes, those with higher copy numbers of a certain gene variant probably gained an evolutionary advantage.
paras.zh: 当安第斯土著人的祖先开始种植土豆时，那些具有较高拷贝数的某种基因变异的人可能获得了进化优势。

paras.en: Starting around 10,000 years ago, those with roughly 10 copies or more had a 1.24 percent survival or reproductive advantage per generation.
paras.zh: 从大约 10,000 年前开始，拥有大约 10 个或更多拷贝的个体每代的生存或繁殖优势为 1.24%。

paras.en: That's small, but it's enough to add up over the millennia.
paras.zh: 虽然这个数字很小，但足够几千年加起来了。

paras.en: "Those with lower copy numbers were eliminated from the population over time, perhaps because they had less number of offspring, and the ones with the higher copy numbers remained," said Gokcumen.
paras.zh: “随着时间的推移，那些拷贝数较低的基因被从种群中淘汰，也许是因为它们的后代数量较少，而拷贝数较高的基因则保留下来，”Gokcumen 说。

paras.en: Related: Humans in The Andes Seem to Have Evolved an Unusual Genetic Ability
paras.zh: 相关：安第斯山脉的人类似乎进化出了一种不寻常的遗传能力

paras.en: Adaptations to our environment also run through our very veins. Take humans who live on the Tibetan plateau, for instance.
paras.zh: 对环境的适应也贯穿于我们的血液之中。以生活在青藏高原的人类为例。

paras.en: Here, high-altitude living for more than 10,000 years has led to fascinating adaptations among local communities.
paras.zh: 在这里，一万多年的高海拔生活导致当地社区发生了令人着迷的适应。

paras.en: For years now, anthropologist Cynthia Beall of Case Western Reserve University in the US has been studying how the human body responds to a lack of oxygen at high altitude.
paras.zh: 多年来，美国凯斯西储大学的人类学家辛西娅·比尔一直在研究人体对高海拔缺氧的反应。

paras.en: In 2024, she and her team reported evidence showing that Tibetan communities possess adaptive traits that improve their blood's ability to deliver oxygen.
paras.zh: 2024 年，她和她的团队报告的证据表明，藏族社区拥有提高血液输送氧气能力的适应性特征。

paras.en: "This is a case of ongoing natural selection," Beall said at the time.
paras.zh: “这是一个持续的自然选择的例子，”比尔当时说。

paras.en: The example is especially strong given the association with reproduction.
paras.zh: 考虑到与繁殖的联系，这个例子尤其有力。

paras.en: Among 417 Nepalese women who had lived their entire lives at altitudes above 3,500 meters (11,480 feet), those who demonstrated the highest rate of live births showed red blood cells with unusually high oxygen saturation.
paras.zh: 在 417 名终生生活在海拔 3,500 米（11,480 英尺）以上的尼泊尔妇女中，活产率最高的妇女的红细胞氧饱和度异常高。

paras.en: "We knew that higher oxygen saturation of hemoglobin was beneficial; now we understand that the higher the saturation, the more beneficial," Beall told ScienceAlert's Michelle Starr.
paras.zh: “我们知道血红蛋白的氧饱和度越高是有益的；现在我们知道饱和度越高，就越有益，”比尔告诉 ScienceAlert 的米歇尔·斯塔尔。

paras.en: "The number of live births quantifies the benefits."
paras.zh: “活产数量可以量化效益。”

paras.en: Some signs of natural selection can also be seen on the outside of our bodies.
paras.zh: 自然选择的一些迹象也可以在我们身体的外部看到。

paras.en: Skin pigmentation, for instance, is a commonly cited example of our species' adaptation to sun exposure.
paras.zh: 例如，皮肤色素沉着是我们物种适应阳光照射的一个常见例子。

paras.en: It is widely accepted that early humans in Africa had darker skin because it provided protection against DNA damage from strong ultraviolet radiation.
paras.zh: 人们普遍认为，非洲早期人类的皮肤较黑，因为它可以保护DNA免受强烈紫外线辐射的损害。

paras.en: But farther from the equator, selective pressures seem to favor lighter skin.
paras.zh: 但在远离赤道的地方，选择性压力似乎有利于浅色皮肤。

paras.en: This year, the largest ancient DNA dataset yet revealed evidence of natural selection among West Eurasians.
paras.zh: 今年，迄今为止最大的古代 DNA 数据集揭示了西欧亚人种自然选择的证据。

paras.en: Nearly 500 gene variants were identified in this lineage that had changed in the last 10,000 years.
paras.zh: 在这个谱系中发现了近 500 个基因变异，这些变异在过去 10,000 年间发生了变化。

paras.en: Many corresponded to known physiological traits, such as body fat, celiac disease, or schizophrenia.
paras.zh: 许多与已知的生理特征相对应，例如身体脂肪、乳糜泻或精神分裂症。

paras.en: But one of the strongest signals of evolution in the dataset concerned skin pigmentation.
paras.zh: 但数据集中最强烈的进化信号之一与皮肤色素沉着有关。

paras.en: Over the past 10,000 years, the results suggest that gene variants associated with lighter pigmentation have become more common in this human population.
paras.zh: 在过去的一万年里，研究结果表明，与较浅色素沉着相关的基因变异在这个人群中变得更加普遍。

paras.en: "This plausibly reflects selection for increased synthesis of vitamin D in regions of low sunlight in farmers with little of it in their diets," the authors suggest.
paras.zh: 作者表示：“这似乎反映出，在日照不足的地区，饮食中维生素 D 含量很少的农民选择了增加维生素 D 的合成。”

paras.en: Even the way that you are reading this article right now might be a product of natural selection.
paras.zh: 甚至您现在阅读本文的方式也可能是自然选择的产物。

paras.en: Myopia, or nearsightedness, has surged in the past few decades.
paras.zh: 近几十年来，近视度数激增。

paras.en: In 2021, researchers found evidence in the UK Biobank that the condition is associated with mutant alleles.
paras.zh: 2021 年，研究人员在英国生物银行发现了证据，表明这种情况与突变等位基因有关。

paras.en: These alleles have increased in frequency over the past 25 years, possibly because of natural selection.
paras.zh: 在过去 25 年里，这些等位基因的出现频率有所增加，这可能是由于自然选择的缘故。

paras.en: While nearsightedness might be a disadvantage for survival, some of the gene variants linked to this trait may have other advantages for reproduction.
paras.zh: 虽然近视可能不利于生存，但与该性状相关的一些基因变异可能对繁殖具有其他优势。

paras.en: This is called 'antagonistic pleiotropy'. It's an evolutionary theory that certain genes confer beneficial effects in early life, but cause detrimental effects later on.
paras.zh: 这称为“拮抗多效性”。这是一种进化理论，认为某些基因在生命早期会产生有益的影响，但随后会产生有害的影响。

paras.en: "We estimate that, in the UK alone, natural selection adds more than 100,000 myopia cases per generation, and argue that antagonistic pleiotropy be broadly considered in explaining the spreads of apparently disadvantageous phenotypes in humans and beyond," the authors of the 2021 study concluded.
paras.zh: 2021 年研究的作者总结道：“我们估计，仅在英国，自然选择每代就增加了超过 10 万例近视病例，并认为拮抗性多效性可广泛考虑解释明显不利的表型在人类及其他地区的传播。”

paras.en: Evolution doesn't always make us healthier or fitter.
paras.zh: 进化并不总是让我们变得更健康或更健康。

paras.en: Related: The 'Shadow' in Evolution That Explains Why Long Life Comes at a Cost
paras.zh: 相关：进化中的“阴影”解释了为什么长寿是有代价的

paras.en: Natural selection favors genes that help us survive, but sometimes, they can drag along other traits that are not so advantageous.
paras.zh: 自然选择有利于帮助我们生存的基因，但有时，它们也会拖累其他不太有利的特征。

paras.en: As the modern world continues to shapeshift around us, so too will the evolutionary pressures shaping our species.
paras.zh: 随着我们周围的现代世界不断发生变化，塑造我们物种的进化压力也将发生变化。

articles.title: Scientists Identified 10 Healthy Diets Linked to Slower Biological Aging
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: We're all well aware that healthy diets are good for us in a multitude of different ways, and a new study published in Nature Communications highlights 10 diet regimes that were linked to slower biological aging in the people who stuck to them.
paras.zh: 我们都清楚，健康饮食在很多方面对我们都有好处，《自然通讯》上发表的一项新研究强调了 10 种饮食习惯，这些饮食习惯与坚持健康饮食的人延缓生物衰老有关。

paras.en: Biological aging is how quickly or slowly our bodies are wearing out, and it doesn't necessarily match up with how many birthdays you've had. Faster aging tends to mean a shorter lifespan, and more health problems in later years.
paras.zh: 生物衰老是指我们的身体磨损的速度有多快或有多慢，它不一定与您度过了多少个生日相匹配。更快的衰老往往意味着更短的寿命，以及晚年更多的健康问题。

paras.en: In this latest study, researchers led by a team from the German Centre for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE) analyzed data for 6,470 participants aged 30 and over, comparing their scores across the 10 sets of diet guidelines with blood biomarkers that indicate biological age.
paras.zh: 在这项最新研究中，由德国神经退行性疾病中心 (DZNE) 团队领导的研究人员分析了 6,470 名 30 岁及以上参与者的数据，将他们在 10 套饮食指南中的得分与表明生物年龄的血液生物标志物进行了比较。

paras.en: Across the board, and all of the diet regimes covered by the study, healthier eating was associated with slower biological aging.
paras.zh: 总体而言，以及该研究涵盖的所有饮食方案，更健康的饮食与减缓生物衰老有关。

paras.en: "The effects are not massive, but they are measurable and relevant for prevention," says epidemiologist Monique Breteler, from DZNE. "By slowing the aging process, the risk of age-related diseases such as dementia or cardiovascular disorders can be reduced."
paras.zh: DZNE 的流行病学家莫妮克·布雷特勒 (Monique Breteler) 表示：“影响并不大，但可以测量，并且与预防相关。” “通过减缓衰老过程，可以降低患痴呆症或心血管疾病等与年龄相关的疾病的风险。”

paras.en: "According to our data, various dietary patterns are associated with slower aging, some more, some less. That is an encouraging finding, because it leaves room to tailor healthy eating to personal and cultural preferences, budget and taste."
paras.zh: “根据我们的数据，不同的饮食模式与衰老速度减缓有关，有的较多，有的较少。这是一个令人鼓舞的发现，因为它为根据个人和文化偏好、预算和口味定制健康饮食留下了空间。”

paras.en: The diets picked by the researchers were already well established as guidelines. They included the Mediterranean diet, the Nordic diet, the DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) diet for lowering blood pressure, and the MIND (Mediterranean-DASH Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay) diet for supporting brain health.
paras.zh: 研究人员选择的饮食已经被明确作为指导方针。其中包括地中海饮食、北欧饮食、用于降低血压的 DASH（止高血压饮食方法）饮食，以及用于支持大脑健康的 MIND（地中海 DASH 神经退行性延迟干预）饮食。

paras.en: There was also the Alternate Healthy Eating Index (AHEI-2010), the Plant-based Diet Index (PDI), the Healthful Plant-based Diet Index (hPDI), and the EAT-Lancet Diet.
paras.zh: 还有替代健康饮食指数 (AHEI-2010)、植物性饮食指数 (PDI)、健康植物性饮食指数 (hPDI) 和 EAT-柳叶刀饮食。

paras.en: The final two diets, the Unhealthful Plant-based Diet Index (uPDI) and the Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII), actually measure unhealthy eating (think sugary drinks and sweets). With these diets, lower scores (so a lower adherence to them) were associated with slower aging.
paras.zh: 最后两种饮食，不健康植物性饮食指数（uPDI）和饮食炎症指数（DII），实际上衡量的是不健康饮食（想想含糖饮料和糖果）。对于这些饮食，较低的分数（因此对它们的坚持程度较低）与较慢的衰老有关。

paras.en: For the aging biomarkers, the researchers were looking at DNA methylation patterns – essentially the changes in chemical tags known to alter with biological age.
paras.zh: 对于衰老生物标志物，研究人员正在研究 DNA 甲基化模式——本质上是已知随生物年龄而改变的化学标签的变化。

paras.en: "We applied three different approaches, so-called epigenetic clocks, to read biological aging from DNA methylation," says epidemiologist Juliana Tavares, from DZNE.
paras.zh: “我们应用了三种不同的方法，即所谓的表观遗传时钟，从 DNA 甲基化中读取生物衰老信息，”DZNE 的流行病学家朱莉安娜·塔瓦雷斯 (Juliana Tavares) 说。

paras.en: "To this end, we leveraged state-of-the-art technology, which allowed us to cover about 850,000 sites in the DNA. This is roughly twice as many as in most previous studies."
paras.zh: “为此，我们利用了最先进的技术，使我们能够覆盖 DNA 中约 850,000 个位点。这大约是之前大多数研究的两倍。”

paras.en: It's worth noting that hardly any of the participants hit high health scores on every set of dietary guidelines. It seems you only need to pick one of these to reduce the risk of your biological age getting ahead of your chronological age.
paras.zh: 值得注意的是，几乎没有参与者在每一套饮食指南上都达到了很高的健康分数。看来您只需要选择其中之一即可降低您的生物学年龄超过实际年龄的风险。

paras.en: While there were some differences in terms of which diets affected which aspects of biological aging – the heart for the DASH diet, and cognition and memory for the MIND diet, for instance – there was also a substantial amount of overlap.
paras.zh: 虽然在哪些饮食影响生物衰老的哪些方面方面存在一些差异（例如，DASH 饮食影响心脏，而 MIND 饮食影响认知和记忆），但也存在大量重叠。

paras.en: "More than 70 percent of the affected biological pathways were shared across all diets," says Tavares. "These involve cell structure, cell signaling and metabolism – processes central to aging and chronic disease."
paras.zh: “超过 70% 的受影响的生物途径在所有饮食中都是相同的，”Tavares 说。 “这些涉及细胞结构、细胞信号传导和新陈代谢——衰老和慢性疾病的核心过程。”

paras.en: The results of the study were verified using a separate sample of 1,034 individuals, analyzed in the same way as the first group. The same associations emerged, broadly speaking: healthier eating meant slower biological aging.
paras.zh: 研究结果通过 1,034 名个体的单独样本进行验证，分析方式与第一组相同。从广义上讲，同样的关联也出现了：更健康的饮食意味着更慢的生物衰老。

paras.en: That said, the research doesn't show direct cause and effect, only a substantial link. The collected data represents a snapshot in time, and further studies could look at how diet changes over an extended period affect DNA methylation.
paras.zh: 也就是说，这项研究并没有显示直接的因果关系，只是显示了实质性的联系。收集到的数据代表了时间的快照，进一步的研究可以研究长期饮食变化如何影响 DNA 甲基化。

paras.en: "You don't need a perfect diet – that may be the most practical message here. But moving forward, the diet-specific pathways point to future research on targeted dietary interventions," says Tavares.
paras.zh: “你不需要完美的饮食——这可能是这里最实用的信息。但展望未来，饮食特定的途径指出了未来有针对性的饮食干预的研究，”塔瓦雷斯说。

paras.en: "This could be helpful in designing targeted health recommendations."
paras.zh: “这可能有助于设计有针对性的健康建议。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Nature Communications.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《自然通讯》上。

articles.title: A compound hidden in broccoli could help fight a devastating genetic disease

paras.en: A compound hidden in broccoli could help fight a devastating genetic disease
paras.zh: 西兰花中隐藏的化合物可以帮助对抗毁灭性的遗传病

paras.en: - A compound naturally found in broccoli could help fight Friedreich ataxia, a devastating genetic disease that progressively damages the nervous system, by boosting a vital protein and protecting nerve cells. Scientists hope the discovery could lead to an affordable treatment, although clinical trials are still needed to establish its effectiveness in patients.
paras.zh: - 西兰花中天然存在的一种化合物可以通过增强重要蛋白质和保护神经细胞来帮助对抗弗里德赖希共济失调，这是一种破坏性遗传疾病，会逐渐损害神经系统。科学家们希望这一发现能够带来一种负担得起的治疗方法，尽管仍需要临床试验来确定其对患者的有效性。

paras.en: A natural substance found in broccoli could offer an unexpected new approach to treating a devastating genetic disease that progressively damages the nervous system. Researchers at Swinburne University have identified promising effects from the compound, raising hopes for a more affordable and accessible treatment for patients with few available options.
paras.zh: 西兰花中发现的一种天然物质可以提供一种意想不到的新方法来治疗一种逐渐损害神经系统的毁灭性遗传疾病。斯威本大学的研究人员已经发现该化合物具有良好的效果，为缺乏选择的患者提供更实惠、更容易的治疗带来了希望。

paras.en: The disease, known as Friedreich ataxia, causes nerve cells in the brain and spinal cord to gradually deteriorate. As the damage progresses, patients lose their ability to coordinate movements, walk, and speak. The condition can also shorten life expectancy, and there is currently no cure. Approximately 200 Australians are living with the disease.
paras.zh: 这种疾病被称为弗里德赖希共济失调，会导致大脑和脊髓中的神经细胞逐渐恶化。随着损伤的进展，患者失去协调运动、行走和说话的能力。这种情况还会缩短预期寿命，目前尚无治愈方法。大约 200 名澳大利亚人患有这种疾病。

paras.en: In a new study, scientists found that sulforaphane, a naturally occurring compound in broccoli, can increase levels of frataxin, a protein that is present in insufficient amounts in people with Friedreich ataxia. The researchers also found that the compound can help protect vulnerable nerve cells from damage.
paras.zh: 在一项新的研究中，科学家发现西兰花中天然存在的化合物萝卜硫素可以增加 frataxin 的水平，而 frataxin 是一种蛋白质，在弗里德赖希共济失调患者中含量不足。研究人员还发现，这种化合物可以帮助保护脆弱的神经细胞免受损伤。

paras.en: How a Broccoli Compound Could Protect Nerve Cells
paras.zh: 西兰花化合物如何保护神经细胞

paras.en: Frataxin plays an important role in keeping cells functioning properly, particularly those with high energy demands, such as nerve cells. In Friedreich ataxia, a genetic defect leads to reduced production of this essential protein, contributing to the progressive damage that characterizes the disease.
paras.zh: Frataxin 在保持细胞正常功能方面发挥着重要作用，特别是那些能量需求较高的细胞，例如神经细胞。在弗里德赖希共济失调中，遗传缺陷导致这种必需蛋白质的产生减少，从而导致该疾病特征的进行性损伤。

paras.en: Sulforaphane appears promising because its potential benefits extend beyond increasing frataxin levels. Research indicates that it can also influence several biological processes involved in disease progression, including cellular stress and inflammation. Addressing multiple sources of damage at once could make the compound a valuable candidate for further investigation.
paras.zh: 萝卜硫素似乎很有前途，因为它的潜在好处不仅仅限于提高 frataxin 水平。研究表明，它还可以影响疾病进展中的多种生物过程，包括细胞应激和炎症。同时解决多个损害源可能会使该化合物成为进一步调查的有价值的候选者。

paras.en: The findings are particularly encouraging for children with Friedreich ataxia. According to lead researcher Associate Professor Faith Kwa of Swinburne University, children account for a large proportion of those affected, yet no treatments specifically approved for pediatric patients are currently available.
paras.zh: 这些发现对于患有弗里德赖希共济失调的儿童来说尤其令人鼓舞。斯威本大学首席研究员 Faith Kwa 副教授表示，儿童在受影响人群中占很大比例，但目前还没有专门批准用于儿童患者的治疗方法。

paras.en: "Friedreich ataxia is a devastating rare genetic disease that progressively steals a child's ability to walk, speak, play, and ultimately survive," she says.
paras.zh: “弗里德赖希共济失调是一种毁灭性的罕见遗传病，它会逐渐剥夺孩子行走、说话、玩耍并最终生存的能力，”她说。

paras.en: "This novel therapeutic agent can target the underlying cause of the disease, while delivering an affordable and accessible therapy worldwide, improving treatment opportunities for families affected by this life-limiting disease.
paras.zh: “这种新型治疗剂可以针对疾病的根本原因，同时在全球范围内提供负担得起且易于使用的治疗方法，从而为受这种致命疾病影响的家庭增加治疗机会。

paras.en: "This discovery brings us closer to a future where children with Friedreich ataxia experience a better quality of life, greater independence, and an improved chance of long-term survival."
paras.zh: “这一发现使我们更接近未来，让患有弗里德赖希共济失调的儿童体验到更好的生活质量、更大的独立性和更高的长期生存机会。”

paras.en: A Potential Treatment That Could Be More Accessible
paras.zh: 一种更容易获得的潜在治疗方法

paras.en: One of the most encouraging aspects of sulforaphane is that it is not an entirely unfamiliar substance. The compound already has an established safety record in both children and adults, and purified, biologically active forms are commercially available.
paras.zh: 萝卜硫素最令人鼓舞的方面之一是它并不是一种完全陌生的物质。该化合物已在儿童和成人中拥有既定的安全记录，并且纯化的生物活性形式已在市场上出售。

paras.en: These advantages could make it easier to develop a widely accessible treatment if future clinical trials confirm that sulforaphane is effective against Friedreich ataxia. However, further research is essential before scientists can determine whether the promising findings will translate into meaningful benefits for patients.
paras.zh: 如果未来的临床试验证实萝卜硫素对弗里德赖希共济失调有效，这些优势可能会使开发一种广泛使用的治疗方法变得更加容易。然而，在科学家确定这些有希望的发现是否会转化为对患者有意义的益处之前，还需要进一步的研究。

paras.en: Kwa explains that the rarity of Friedreich ataxia creates additional challenges for researchers. Because relatively few people have the disease, public awareness is limited, making it more difficult to attract the funding needed to investigate potential treatments.
paras.zh: Kwa 解释说，弗里德赖希共济失调的罕见性给研究人员带来了额外的挑战。由于患有这种疾病的人相对较少，公众的认识有限，因此更难以吸引研究潜在治疗方法所需的资金。

paras.en: Researchers Seek Funding for Clinical Trials
paras.zh: 研究人员寻求临床试验资金

paras.en: The Swinburne team hopes to secure financial support for clinical trials that would examine whether sulforaphane can deliver the same promising effects in people living with the disease.
paras.zh: 斯威本团队希望为临床试验获得财政支持，该试验将检查萝卜硫素是否可以为患有这种疾病的人带来同样有希望的效果。

paras.en: "We are hoping to gain funding to conduct clinical trials and further prove the positive impact the broccoli compound could have on those suffering from Friedreich ataxia," she says.
paras.zh: “我们希望获得资金来进行临床试验，并进一步证明西兰花化合物对弗里德赖希共济失调患者可能产生的积极影响，”她说。

paras.en: "Sulforaphane already has an established safety record in children and adults, and its pure and bioactive form is commercially available. This means if clinical trials prove successful, its rollout could accelerate the path to patient impact."
paras.zh: “萝卜硫素已经在儿童和成人中拥有既定的安全记录，其纯净的生物活性形式已上市。这意味着，如果临床试验证明成功，它的推出可能会加速对患者产生影响的道路。”

paras.en: For patients and families facing a progressive illness with no cure, even improvements in everyday functioning and independence could make a meaningful difference. The researchers hope their work will not only advance treatment possibilities but also bring greater attention to a condition that remains largely unknown to the public.
paras.zh: 对于面临无法治愈的进行性疾病的患者和家庭来说，即使日常功能和独立性的改善也可能产生有意义的变化。研究人员希望他们的工作不仅能提高治疗的可能性，还能让人们更多地关注这种公众仍不了解的疾病。

paras.en: "Even if we can raise awareness of this debilitating condition or improve one person's quality of life, our efforts will have been worth it."
paras.zh: “即使我们能够提高人们对这种令人衰弱的状况的认识或改善一个人的生活质量，我们的努力也是值得的。”

paras.en: Materials provided by Swinburne University of Technology. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由斯威本科技大学提供。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

paras.en: - Wenyao Yang, Bruce Thompson, Sara Miellet, Marnie Maddock, Marek Napierala, Mirella Dottori, Faith A.A. Kwa. Unlocking Sulforaphaneâs Potential in Friedreich Ataxia: Further Evidence from Preclinical Investigations Using Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell-Derived Sensory Neurons. Antioxidants, 2026; 45 (13-15): 561 DOI: 10.1177/15230864261470377
paras.zh: - Wenyao Yang、Bruce Thompson、Sara Miellet、Marnie Maddock、Marek Napierala、Mirella Dottori、Faith A.A.夸。解锁萝卜硫素在弗里德赖希共济失调中的潜力：使用诱导多能干细胞衍生的感觉神经元进行临床前研究的进一步证据。抗氧化剂，2026； 45 (13-15): 561 DOI: 10.1177/15230864261470377

articles.title: Magic mushrooms rewire the brain in a way scientists didn't expect

paras.en: Magic mushrooms rewire the brain in a way scientists didn't expect
paras.zh: 神奇蘑菇以科学家意想不到的方式重塑大脑

paras.en: - A surprising discovery reveals how psilocybin, the active compound in magic mushrooms, rapidly reshapes the brain by creating new neural connections and strengthening them. Researchers found that the drug behaves differently in healthy and chronically stressed mice, potentially helping repair brain circuits damaged by prolonged stress. Most intriguingly, they identified a way to trigger this brain rewiring without the behavioral response associated with psychedelic effects.
paras.zh: - 一项令人惊讶的发现揭示了迷幻蘑菇中的活性化合物裸盖菇素如何通过创建新的神经连接并强化它们来快速重塑大脑。研究人员发现，该药物在健康小鼠和长期承受压力的小鼠中表现不同，可能有助于修复因长期压力而受损的大脑回路。最有趣的是，他们找到了一种触发大脑重新布线的方法，而无需产生与迷幻效果相关的行为反应。

paras.en: A new study from the University of California, Santa Cruz, has revealed how psilocybin, the psychedelic substance found in "magic mushrooms," changes the brain by reorganizing connections between nerve cells. The findings could eventually help scientists develop treatments for mental health conditions that capture some of psilocybin's potential benefits without producing hallucinations.
paras.zh: 加州大学圣克鲁斯分校的一项新研究揭示了“迷幻蘑菇”中发现的迷幻物质裸盖菇素如何通过重组神经细胞之间的连接来改变大脑。这些发现最终可能帮助科学家开发出治疗精神健康状况的疗法，在不产生幻觉的情况下捕捉裸盖菇素的一些潜在益处。

paras.en: The research, published October 15 in Nature Neuroscience, found that psilocybin rapidly encourages brain cells to form new connections and helps those connections mature. At the same time, it promotes the removal of certain older connections, suggesting that its effects involve more than simply increasing communication between neurons.
paras.zh: 该研究于 10 月 15 日发表在《自然神经科学》杂志上，发现裸盖菇素能迅速促进脑细胞形成新的连接，并帮助这些连接成熟。同时，它促进某些旧连接的去除，这表明它的作用不仅仅是增加神经元之间的交流。

paras.en: Experiments in mice also revealed something especially intriguing. The researchers were able to separate the cellular changes responsible for this rewiring from a behavioral response commonly associated with psychedelic effects. This suggests that some of psilocybin's effects on brain structure may be achievable without the hallucinations typically associated with the drug.
paras.zh: 小鼠实验还揭示了一些特别有趣的事情。研究人员能够将导致这种重新布线的细胞变化与通常与迷幻效果相关的行为反应区分开来。这表明裸盖菇素对大脑结构的一些影响可能是可以实现的，而不会产生通常与该药物相关的幻觉。

paras.en: The discovery could provide a foundation for developing medications that enhance the brain's ability to adapt and reorganize itself, a property known as neuroplasticity. Such treatments might eventually offer new approaches for depression, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), and other psychiatric conditions.
paras.zh: 这一发现可以为开发增强大脑自我适应和重组能力的药物奠定基础，这种能力被称为神经可塑性。此类治疗最终可能为抑郁症、创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）和其他精神疾病提供新方法。

paras.en: The team also identified a particular group of neurons in the cerebral cortex that plays an essential role in psilocybin's effects on brain connections. Importantly, the researchers discovered that the drug does not affect every brain in the same way. Its influence depends partly on whether the brain has previously experienced chronic stress.
paras.zh: 研究小组还发现了大脑皮层中的一组特定神经元，它们在裸盖菇素对大脑连接的影响中发挥着重要作用。重要的是，研究人员发现该药物不会以相同的方式影响每个大脑。它的影响部分取决于大脑之前是否经历过慢性压力。

paras.en: "I consider this work a major advance, particularly in our understanding of how psilocybin reshapes neural circuits and its potential implications for treating mental disorders," said senior author Yi Zuo, professor of molecular, cell, and developmental biology at UC Santa Cruz.
paras.zh: “我认为这项工作是一项重大进展，特别是在我们了解裸盖菇素如何重塑神经回路及其对治疗精神障碍的潜在影响方面，”资深作者、加州大学圣克鲁斯分校分子、细胞和发育生物学教授 Yi Zuo 说。

paras.en: Why Scientists Are Taking a New Look at Psychedelics
paras.zh: 为什么科学家们正在重新审视迷幻药

paras.en: Scientific interest in psychedelic drugs has changed dramatically over the past century. During the middle of the 20th century, substances such as psilocybin and LSD attracted attention from Western researchers because of their powerful effects on perception, consciousness, and mood.
paras.zh: 在过去的一个世纪里，科学界对迷幻药物的兴趣发生了巨大的变化。 20世纪中叶，裸盖菇素和LSD等物质因其对知觉、意识和情绪的强大影响而引起了西方研究人员的关注。

paras.en: Early studies suggested these compounds might have applications in psychiatric treatment. However, scientific investigations slowed substantially after the United States passed the Controlled Substances Act in 1970, which imposed strict restrictions on these substances.
paras.zh: 早期研究表明这些化合物可能在精神病治疗中具有应用价值。然而，在美国于 1970 年通过《受控物质法案》后，科学调查大幅放缓，该法案对这些物质实施了严格限制。

paras.en: In recent years, researchers have renewed their interest in psychedelics, particularly their ability to produce rapid and potentially lasting changes in brain function.
paras.zh: 近年来，研究人员重新燃起了对致幻剂的兴趣，特别是它们对大脑功能产生快速且可能持久的变化的能力。

paras.en: Scientists sometimes describe these compounds as "psychoplastogens" because they can stimulate neuroplasticity after a single dose. Neuroplasticity refers to the brain's capacity to change its structure and activity by forming, strengthening, reorganizing, or removing connections between neurons.
paras.zh: 科学家有时将这些化合物描述为“精神塑性剂”，因为它们在单次剂量后可以刺激神经可塑性。神经可塑性是指大脑通过形成、加强、重组或消除神经元之间的连接来改变其结构和活动的能力。

paras.en: This property is particularly interesting for mental health treatment because conditions such as depression can involve disruptions in the circuits responsible for regulating mood, emotions, and behavior.
paras.zh: 这一特性对于心理健康治疗特别有趣，因为抑郁症等疾病可能会导致负责调节情绪、情绪和行为的回路受到干扰。

paras.en: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has previously recognized the therapeutic potential of psychedelic research by granting Breakthrough Therapy designations to substances including psilocybin and MDMA. These designations are intended to accelerate the development and review of promising treatments for serious medical conditions.
paras.zh: 美国食品和药物管理局 (FDA) 此前已认识到致幻剂研究的治疗潜力，授予裸盖菇素和 MDMA 等物质突破性疗法称号。这些指定旨在加速开发和审查有前景的严重疾病治疗方法。

paras.en: In September 2026, the FDA took another step toward evaluating psychedelic treatments by organizing a public hearing titled "Considerations for Potential Future Therapeutic Use of Psychedelic Drugs."
paras.zh: 2026 年 9 月，FDA 在评估迷幻药物治疗方面又迈出了一步，组织了一次题为“迷幻药物未来潜在治疗用途的考虑因素”的公开听证会。

paras.en: Experts discussed how healthcare professionals administering psychedelic treatments should be qualified, how potential risks could be managed through Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) programs, and how future clinical trials should be designed.
paras.zh: 专家们讨论了实施迷幻治疗的医疗保健专业人员应如何获得资格、如何通过风险评估和缓解策略（REMS）计划来管理潜在风险，以及应如何设计未来的临床试验。

paras.en: As regulators examine ways psychedelic treatments might eventually become part of mainstream healthcare, researchers are increasingly focused on understanding exactly what these substances do to the brain. Identifying the cellular mechanisms behind their effects could help scientists develop treatments that are both effective and safer to administer.
paras.zh: 随着监管机构研究致幻剂治疗最终可能成为主流医疗保健一部分的方式，研究人员越来越专注于了解这些物质对大脑的确切作用。确定其作用背后的细胞机制可以帮助科学家开发出既有效又安全的治疗方法。

paras.en: To investigate how psilocybin changes brain structure, the UC Santa Cruz team used an advanced imaging method called two-photon microscopy.
paras.zh: 为了研究裸盖菇素如何改变大脑结构，加州大学圣克鲁斯分校团队使用了一种称为双光子显微镜的先进成像方法。

paras.en: This technology allows scientists to observe extremely small structures inside living tissue with remarkable detail. Using it, the researchers followed individual connections on neurons in living mice over several weeks, allowing them to see how those structures changed after psilocybin treatment.
paras.zh: 这项技术使科学家能够以非凡的细节观察活体组织内的极小结构。利用它，研究人员在几周内追踪了活体小鼠神经元的个体连接，使他们能够看到这些结构在裸盖菇素治疗后如何变化。

paras.en: Their attention centered on tiny projections called dendritic spines. These structures extend from neurons and receive messages from neighboring nerve cells. They help form synapses, the specialized junctions through which neurons communicate.
paras.zh: 他们的注意力集中在称为树突棘的微小突起上。这些结构从神经元延伸并接收来自邻近神经细胞的信息。它们有助于形成突触，即神经元进行交流的特殊连接点。

paras.en: Synapses are essential for processing information and supporting functions such as learning, memory, and emotional regulation. Changes in their number, strength, and organization can alter the way information travels through the brain.
paras.zh: 突触对于处理信息和支持学习、记忆和情绪调节等功能至关重要。它们的数量、强度和组织的变化可以改变信息在大脑中传播的方式。

paras.en: Within just 24 hours of psilocybin administration, the researchers observed a substantial increase in newly forming dendritic spines.
paras.zh: 在服用裸盖菇素后的短短 24 小时内，研究人员就观察到新形成的树突棘大幅增加。

paras.en: But the drug did more than encourage new connections to appear. It also helped them develop into more mature structures at an unusually rapid pace.
paras.zh: 但这种药物的作用不仅仅是鼓励新联系的出现。它还帮助他们以异常快的速度发展成更成熟的结构。

paras.en: Normally, newly formed spines often begin as small, immature structures described as "stubby." Many remain unstable and disappear before becoming fully developed connections.
paras.zh: 通常，新形成的刺通常以小的、不成熟的结构开始，被称为“粗短”。许多连接仍然不稳定并在完全发展之前消失。

paras.en: After psilocybin treatment, however, a much larger proportion developed into structures with a distinctive "mushroom" appearance. These mature spines are generally more stable and contain higher concentrations of receptors that receive chemical signals from neighboring neurons.
paras.zh: 然而，经过裸盖菇素处理后，更大的比例发育成具有独特“蘑菇”外观的结构。这些成熟的棘通常更稳定，并且含有更高浓度的受体，可以接收来自邻近神经元的化学信号。

paras.en: Because of these features, mature spines can support stronger and more persistent communication between brain cells, potentially contributing to lasting changes in circuits involved in memory and mood.
paras.zh: 由于这些特征，成熟的脊柱可以支持脑细胞之间更强大、更持久的沟通，可能有助于记忆和情绪相关回路的持久变化。

paras.en: For lead author Jacob Baker, one of the biggest questions is whether these structural changes require the intense psychedelic experience typically produced by psilocybin.
paras.zh: 对于主要作者雅各布·贝克（Jacob Baker）来说，最大的问题之一是这些结构变化是否需要通常由裸盖菇素产生的强烈迷幻体验。

paras.en: "Psychedelics are fascinating compounds because they have the potential to profoundly transform who we are by reshaping the neural circuits in our brains," said Baker, a Ph.D. student in Zuo's lab.
paras.zh: “迷幻药是令人着迷的化合物，因为它们有可能通过重塑我们大脑中的神经回路来深刻改变我们的身份，”博士贝克说。左实验室的学生。

paras.en: "These newly formed connections can integrate into existing neural circuitry and persist over time, leaving a lasting structural trace of psilocybin's effects on the brain."
paras.zh: “这些新形成的连接可以整合到现有的神经回路中，并随着时间的推移持续存在，留下裸盖菇素对大脑影响的持久结构痕迹。”

paras.en: Psilocybin Affects Healthy and Stressed Brains Differently
paras.zh: 裸盖菇素对健康和压力大脑的影响不同

paras.en: One of the study's most revealing findings was that psilocybin's influence on brain connections changed depending on whether the mice had experienced prolonged stress.
paras.zh: 该研究最有启发性的发现之一是，裸盖菇素对大脑连接的影响会根据小鼠是否经历长期压力而变化。

paras.en: In healthy mice, psilocybin initially stimulated the formation of new dendritic spines. Over the following three weeks, however, the number of connections gradually moved back toward its previous level.
paras.zh: 在健康小鼠中，裸盖菇素最初刺激了新树突棘的形成。然而，在接下来的三周内，连接数量逐渐恢复到之前的水平。

paras.en: This happened partly because the brain eliminated some connections that had existed before treatment. Rather than simply accumulating additional synapses, the healthy brain appeared to reorganize its existing circuitry while maintaining an overall balance.
paras.zh: 发生这种情况的部分原因是大脑消除了治疗前存在的一些连接。健康的大脑似乎不是简单地积累额外的突触，而是重组其现有的电路，同时保持整体平衡。

paras.en: The researchers observed a different response in mice exposed to chronic stress.
paras.zh: 研究人员观察到暴露于慢性压力的小鼠有不同的反应。

paras.en: To investigate this, they used an unpredictable mild stress model, which exposes animals to varying low-intensity stressors and produces changes that resemble certain features of human depression.
paras.zh: 为了研究这一点，他们使用了一种不可预测的温和应激模型，该模型使动物暴露在不同的低强度应激源下，并产生类似于人类抑郁症某些特征的变化。

paras.en: Prolonged stress is known to interfere with neural communication and can cause substantial losses of synaptic connections. Over time, these changes can weaken the circuits involved in important brain functions.
paras.zh: 众所周知，长时间的压力会干扰神经通讯，并可能导致突触连接的大量损失。随着时间的推移，这些变化会削弱参与重要大脑功能的回路。

paras.en: When the stressed mice received psilocybin, the researchers observed an especially strong increase in the formation of new dendritic spines.
paras.zh: 当受到压力的小鼠接受裸盖菇素时，研究人员观察到新树突棘的形成特别强烈。

paras.en: At the same time, psilocybin prevented the unusually high rate of connection loss associated with chronic stress.
paras.zh: 与此同时，裸盖菇素可以防止与慢性压力相关的异常高的连接丢失率。

paras.en: Together, these effects suggest that psilocybin may do more than temporarily increase the number of connections in the brain. Under stressful conditions, it may also help preserve existing connections and restore circuitry that has been disrupted.
paras.zh: 总之，这些作用表明裸盖菇素的作用可能不仅仅是暂时增加大脑中的连接数量。在压力条件下，它还可能有助于保留现有连接并恢复已中断的电路。

paras.en: "These findings challenge the prevailing view that psilocybin simply increases neural connectivity and suggest that its effects depend on the brain's underlying condition," Zuo added.
paras.zh: Zuo 补充道：“这些发现挑战了普遍的观点，即裸盖菇素只是增加神经连接，并表明其影响取决于大脑的潜在状况。”

paras.en: "This provides a new perspective on how psychedelics might help restore neural circuits disrupted by stress, with potentially important implications for understanding their therapeutic effects in depression and other psychiatric disorders."
paras.zh: “这为迷幻药如何帮助恢复因压力而中断的神经回路提供了新的视角，对于理解其对抑郁症和其他精神疾病的治疗效果具有潜在的重要意义。”

paras.en: Could Psilocybin Rewire the Brain Without Hallucinations?
paras.zh: 赛洛西宾能否在没有幻觉的情况下重塑大脑？

paras.en: Perhaps the most significant implication of the research concerns a longstanding question in psychedelic medicine: Are hallucinations and altered states of consciousness necessary for the brain changes that might contribute to therapeutic benefits?
paras.zh: 也许这项研究最重要的意义涉及迷幻医学中一个长期存在的问题：幻觉和意识状态改变对于可能有助于治疗效果的大脑变化是否是必要的？

paras.en: To explore this possibility, the scientists examined the role of serotonin 2A receptors (5-HT2ARs), which are proteins on the surfaces of cells that respond to chemical signals. These receptors are central to the effects of psilocybin and other classic psychedelics.
paras.zh: 为了探索这种可能性，科学家们研究了血清素 2A 受体 (5-HT2AR) 的作用，这些受体是细胞表面对化学信号做出反应的蛋白质。这些受体对于裸盖菇素和其他经典致幻剂的作用至关重要。

paras.en: The researchers focused on a group of nerve cells called Layer 5 pyramidal neurons. These cells are located in the cerebral cortex, the outer region of the brain involved in complex functions such as perception, reasoning, and decision-making.
paras.zh: 研究人员重点关注一组称为第 5 层锥体神经元的神经细胞。这些细胞位于大脑皮层，大脑的外部区域，参与感知、推理和决策等复杂功能。

paras.en: Layer 5 pyramidal neurons serve as important communication pathways that send information from the cortex to other brain regions. They also contain high levels of serotonin 2A receptors, making them especially relevant to understanding psilocybin's effects.
paras.zh: 第 5 层锥体神经元是重要的通信通路，将信息从皮层发送到其他大脑区域。它们还含有高水平的血清素 2A 受体，这使得它们对于了解裸盖菇素的作用特别重要。

paras.en: Using genetically modified mice, the team selectively changed whether these neurons possessed the receptors.
paras.zh: 研究小组使用基因改造小鼠，选择性地改变这些神经元是否拥有受体。

paras.en: The results revealed a striking separation between changes in brain connections and a behavior associated with psychedelic activity.
paras.zh: 结果显示，大脑连接的变化和与迷幻活动相关的行为之间存在显着的区别。

paras.en: When the researchers restored serotonin 2A receptors only in Layer 5 pyramidal neurons, psilocybin was still able to stimulate the development of new synapses and help stabilize them.
paras.zh: 当研究人员仅在第 5 层锥体神经元中恢复血清素 2A 受体时，裸盖菇素仍然能够刺激新突触的发育并帮助稳定它们。

paras.en: Surprisingly, these mice did not display the characteristic head twitch response that researchers commonly use as an indicator of psychedelic activity in rodents.
paras.zh: 令人惊讶的是，这些小鼠并没有表现出研究人员通常用作啮齿动物迷幻活动指标的特征性头部抽搐反应。

paras.en: The scientists then performed the opposite experiment.
paras.zh: 然后科学家们进行了相反的实验。

paras.en: When they removed serotonin 2A receptors specifically from Layer 5 pyramidal neurons, psilocybin lost its ability to stimulate the same structural growth of synapses.
paras.zh: 当他们专门从第 5 层锥体神经元去除血清素 2A 受体时，裸盖菇素就失去了刺激突触相同结构生长的能力。

paras.en: However, the mice still exhibited the head twitch response.
paras.zh: 然而，小鼠仍然表现出头部抽搐反应。

paras.en: These contrasting results demonstrate that serotonin 2A receptor signaling in Layer 5 pyramidal neurons is necessary and sufficient for the structural brain changes observed in the experiments, while those same receptors are not required for the psychedelic-associated behavioral response.
paras.zh: 这些对比结果表明，第 5 层锥体神经元中的血清素 2A 受体信号传导对于实验中观察到的大脑结构变化是必要且充分的，而与迷幻相关的行为反应则不需要这些相同的受体。

paras.en: In other words, the cellular pathway responsible for psilocybin's brain rewiring can be separated from the pathway responsible for this particular behavioral marker of psychedelic activity.
paras.zh: 换句话说，负责裸盖菇素大脑重新布线的细胞途径可以与负责迷幻活动的这种特定行为标记的途径分开。

paras.en: Because mice cannot describe subjective experiences, the head twitch response does not directly establish whether an animal is experiencing hallucinations. Nevertheless, the findings provide important evidence that these two effects involve distinct cellular mechanisms.
paras.zh: 由于小鼠无法描述主观体验，因此头部抽搐反应并不能直接确定动物是否正在经历幻觉。然而，这些发现提供了重要的证据，证明这两种效应涉及不同的细胞机制。

paras.en: A Potential Path Toward Psychedelic Treatments Without the Trip
paras.zh: 无需旅行即可进行迷幻治疗的潜在途径

paras.en: The discovery could have major implications for the development of future psychiatric medications.
paras.zh: 这一发现可能对未来精神药物的开发产生重大影响。

paras.en: If researchers can identify compounds that activate the brain's ability to rebuild and reorganize neural connections without triggering psychedelic effects, it may become possible to create treatments that preserve some of psilocybin's therapeutic potential while avoiding the need for patients to undergo intense altered states of consciousness.
paras.zh: 如果研究人员能够识别出能够激活大脑重建和重组神经连接的能力而不引发迷幻效应的化合物，那么就有可能创造出保留裸盖菇素部分治疗潜力的治疗方法，同时避免患者经历强烈的意识状态改变。

paras.en: Such medications could be easier to administer and might require less intensive clinical supervision than conventional psychedelic-assisted therapies.
paras.zh: 与传统的迷幻辅助疗法相比，此类药物可能更容易管理，并且可能需要更少的密集临床监督。

paras.en: "By showing that therapeutic circuit remodeling and hallucinogenic effects operate through distinct cellular pathways, our study provides a promising blueprint for designing non-hallucinogenic drug analogs," Zuo said.
paras.zh: “通过表明治疗回路重塑和致幻作用通过不同的细胞途径发挥作用，我们的研究为设计非致幻药物类似物提供了有希望的蓝图，”左说。

paras.en: "Such therapeutics could deliver the fast and lasting antidepressant benefits of psychedelics while eliminating hallucinogenic side effects -- making neuroplasticity treatments safer, more scalable, and accessible to a broader patient population."
paras.zh: “这种疗法可以提供迷幻药快速而持久的抗抑郁功效，同时消除致幻副作用，使神经可塑性治疗更安全、更可扩展，并且可供更广泛的患者群体使用。”

paras.en: Although the results are promising, the experiments were conducted in mice. Additional research will be necessary to determine whether the same cellular mechanisms operate in humans and whether separating brain rewiring from psychedelic effects can produce effective treatments for depression, PTSD, or other psychiatric disorders.
paras.zh: 尽管结果令人鼓舞，但实验是在小鼠身上进行的。还需要进行更多的研究来确定相同的细胞机制是否在人类中发挥作用，以及将大脑重新布线与迷幻作用分开是否可以有效治疗抑郁症、创伤后应激障碍或其他精神疾病。

paras.en: For now, the findings provide a more detailed picture of how psilocybin changes the brain and reveal a potential strategy for harnessing its effects on neural connections without relying on the psychedelic experience itself.
paras.zh: 目前，这些发现提供了裸盖菇素如何改变大脑的更详细图片，并揭示了一种在不依赖迷幻体验本身的情况下利用其对神经连接的影响的潜在策略。

paras.en: The study's other UC Santa Cruz coauthors include molecular and cell biologists Jacob Baker, Emily Kogan, Shaorong Ma, and Ju Lu, alongside Zuo.
paras.zh: 该研究的其他加州大学圣克鲁斯分校的共同作者包括分子和细胞生物学家 Jacob Baker、Emily Kogan、Shaorong Ma 和 Ju Lu，以及 Zuo。

paras.en: Funding came from the National Institute of Mental Health and the National Institute on Aging. The psilocybin used in the experiments was supplied through the National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA) Drug Supply Program.
paras.zh: 资金来自国家心理健康研究所和国家老龄化研究所。实验中使用的裸盖菇素是通过国家药物滥用研究所 (NIDA) 药物供应计划提供的。

paras.en: Materials provided by University of California - Santa Cruz. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由加州大学圣克鲁斯分校提供。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

paras.en: - Jacob J. Baker, Emily Kogan, Shaorong Ma, Ju Lu, Yi Zuo. 5-HT2A receptors in layer 5 pyramidal neurons mediate the neuroplastic but not the hallucinogenic effects of psilocybin. Nature Neuroscience, 2026; DOI: 10.1038/s41593-026-02490-y
paras.zh: - Jacob J. Baker、Emily Kogan、马少荣、Ju Lu、Yi Zuo。第 5 层锥体神经元中的 5-HT2A 受体介导裸盖菇素的神经塑性作用，但不介导致幻作用。自然神经科学，2026； DOI：10.1038/s41593-026-02490-y

articles.title: Rubin Observatory discovers two hidden companions of the Milky Way. Hundreds more may be waiting

paras.en: Rubin Observatory discovers two hidden companions of the Milky Way. Hundreds more may be waiting
paras.zh: 鲁宾天文台发现了银河系的两个隐藏伴星。可能还有数百人在等待

paras.en: - The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has already uncovered two previously unknown companions of the Milky Way using preliminary observations covering just 7% of the night sky. The discoveries include an extremely faint galaxy 355,000 light-years away and a star cluster hidden behind cosmic dust. Scientists suspect hundreds of additional satellite galaxies remain undiscovered, and Rubin's powerful telescope could finally bring them into view.
paras.zh: - Vera C. Rubin 天文台已经通过仅覆盖夜空 7% 的初步观测发现了两个以前未知的银河系伴星。这些发现包括 355,000 光年外的一个极其微弱的星系和一个隐藏在宇宙尘埃后面的星团。科学家怀疑还有数百个卫星星系尚未被发现，而鲁宾强大的望远镜最终可以将它们带入视野。

paras.en: The powerful new Vera C. Rubin Observatory in Chile has already uncovered two previously unknown companions of the Milky Way, offering an early glimpse of what could become a much larger wave of discoveries. Astronomers believe hundreds of faint galaxies may still be hiding around our galaxy, and the observatory could finally bring many of them into view.
paras.zh: 位于智利的强大的新维拉·C·鲁宾天文台已经发现了两个以前未知的银河系伴星，为可能成为更大的发现浪潮提供了早期的一瞥。天文学家认为，数百个微弱的星系可能仍然隐藏在我们的银河系周围，天文台最终可以将其中的许多星系带入视野。

paras.en: Located on Cerro Pachón in the Chilean Andes, the recently completed NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory is designed to explore the sky in extraordinary detail. Its initial observations have now revealed two elusive objects that had escaped detection, demonstrating the telescope's ability to find some of the faintest members of our galactic neighborhood.
paras.zh: 最近竣工的 NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin 天文台位于智利安第斯山脉的帕琼山，旨在以非凡的细节探索天空。它的初步观测现在已经揭示了两个难以捉摸的物体，它们逃脱了探测，这证明了望远镜有能力找到我们银河系附近一些最微弱的成员。

paras.en: Large galaxies such as the Milky Way are surrounded by smaller companions known as satellites. These include dwarf galaxies and star clusters, many of which contain so few stars that they are extremely difficult to detect. Astronomers have identified approximately 65 satellite galaxies around the Milky Way, but some estimates suggest that hundreds more remain undiscovered.
paras.zh: 像银河系这样的大型星系被称为卫星的较小星系包围着。其中包括矮星系和星团，其中许多恒星的恒星数量极少，极难探测到。天文学家已经在银河系周围发现了大约 65 个卫星星系，但一些估计表明还有数百个仍未被发现。

paras.en: Two new studies, including one led by a Yale astronomer, suggest that Rubin could play a major role in finding these missing objects and completing the picture of our galaxy's surroundings.
paras.zh: 两项新研究，其中一项由耶鲁大学天文学家领导，表明鲁宾可以在寻找这些失踪物体和完成银河系周围环境的图像方面发挥重要作用。

paras.en: Two Hidden Companions of the Milky Way Discovered
paras.zh: 银河系的两个隐藏伴侣被发现

paras.en: Using observations collected before the observatory's official launch, researchers identified two exceptionally faint satellites that had never been seen before.
paras.zh: 利用天文台正式发射前收集的观测结果，研究人员发现了两颗以前从未见过的异常​​微弱的卫星。

paras.en: The first, Aquarius IV, is a tiny galaxy located in the distant outskirts of the Milky Way, approximately 355,000 light-years from Earth. The second, Rubin-GC1, is a star cluster on the opposite side of our galaxy, hidden within a region where thick clouds of cosmic dust make observations especially challenging.
paras.zh: 第一个是水瓶座 IV，是一个位于银河系遥远郊区的微小星系，距地球约 355,000 光年。第二个是 Rubin-GC1，是位于银河系另一侧的一个星团，隐藏在一个区域内，那里厚厚的宇宙尘埃云使观测变得特别困难。

paras.en: Both discoveries are remarkable because astronomers made them using only a small amount of the data Rubin is expected to collect over its lifetime.
paras.zh: 这两项发现都是非凡的，因为天文学家只使用了鲁宾在其一生中预计收集的少量数据。

paras.en: "What I find especially exciting is that these discoveries are just the beginning for Rubin," said William Cerny, an astronomy student in Yale's Graduate School of Arts and Sciences.
paras.zh: 耶鲁大学艺术与科学研究生院的天文学学生威廉·塞尔尼说：“我觉得特别令人兴奋的是，这些发现对于鲁宾来说只是一个开始。”

paras.en: Cerny is the lead author of the Aquarius IV study, published in Research Notes of the AAS, and the second author of the Rubin-GC1 study, which has been accepted by The Astrophysical Journal Letters.
paras.zh: Cerny 是 Aquarius IV 研究的第一作者，该研究发表在 AAS 研究笔记上，也是 Rubin-GC1 研究的第二作者，该研究已被《天体物理学杂志快报》接受。

paras.en: "If the observatory can find systems this faint and difficult with only its preview data, its full 10-year survey will undoubtedly provide us with many more Milky Way satellite discoveries," Cerny said. "These new satellites will give us new opportunities to test models of galaxy formation, trace the assembly history of the Milky Way, and investigate the nature of dark matter."
paras.zh: 塞尔尼说：“如果天文台仅凭预览数据就能找到如此微弱和困难的系统，那么其为期十年的调查无疑将为我们提供更多的银河系卫星发现。” “这些新卫星将为我们提供新的机会来测试星系形成模型，追踪银河系的组装历史，并研究暗物质的性质。”

paras.en: A Powerful New Telescope Is Just Getting Started
paras.zh: 强大的新型望远镜才刚刚开始

paras.en: Rubin began its ambitious 10-year Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) in June. The project aims to produce an exceptionally detailed record of the changing night sky while searching for objects that previous telescopes have been unable to detect.
paras.zh: 鲁宾于 6 月开始了雄心勃勃的为期 10 年的时空遗产调查 (LSST)。该项目旨在对不断变化的夜空进行极其详细的记录，同时寻找以前的望远镜无法探测到的物体。

paras.en: One of its major scientific goals is to map the Milky Way's "halo," a vast, roughly spherical region that surrounds the galaxy's main disk. This halo contains scattered stars, gas, and dark matter, along with faint satellite galaxies, star clusters, and other structures that preserve clues about the Milky Way's past.
paras.zh: 它的主要科学目标之一是绘制银河系的“光环”地图，这是一个围绕银河系主盘的巨大的、大致呈球形的区域。这个光环包含分散的恒星、气体和暗物质，以及微弱的卫星星系、星团和其他保留了银河系过去线索的结构。

paras.en: To carry out this enormous survey, Rubin uses the 8.4-meter Simonyi Survey Telescope and the largest digital camera ever constructed, capable of capturing images with 3.2 gigapixels of resolution. By repeatedly photographing large areas of the Southern Hemisphere sky, the observatory will build an extraordinarily wide-ranging time-lapse record of the universe.
paras.zh: 为了进行这项大规模的勘测，鲁宾使用了 8.4 米的西蒙尼勘测望远镜和有史以来最大的数码相机，能够捕捉分辨率为 3.2 十亿像素的图像。通过反复拍摄南半球天空的大片区域，该天文台将建立一个范围极其广泛的宇宙延时记录。

paras.en: The facility is jointly funded by the National Science Foundation and the U.S. Department of Energy's Office of Science.
paras.zh: 该设施由美国国家科学基金会和美国能源部科学办公室共同资助。

paras.en: Just 7% of the Night Sky Revealed Two New Satellites
paras.zh: 只有 7% 的夜空出现了两颗新卫星

paras.en: For the new studies, astronomers examined preview observations gathered between April 2025 and January 2026. These images covered only about 7% of the entire night sky, yet they were sufficient to reveal two previously unknown companions of the Milky Way.
paras.zh: 在这项新研究中，天文学家检查了 2025 年 4 月至 2026 年 1 月期间收集的预览观测结果。这些图像仅覆盖了整个夜空的约 7%，但足以揭示银河系的两个以前未知的伴星。

paras.en: The discoveries offer an encouraging indication of what could emerge as Rubin continues collecting data across a much larger portion of the sky.
paras.zh: 这些发现提供了令人鼓舞的迹象，表明随着鲁宾继续在更大范围的天空中收集数据，可能会出现什么情况。

paras.en: "Finding new Milky Way satellites in Rubin Observatory data has been an exciting future prospect for most of my career," said Marla Geha, a professor of astronomy and physics in Yale's Faculty of Arts and Sciences, and co-author on both studies. "It is remarkable this is now a reality."
paras.zh: 耶鲁大学文理学院天文学和物理学教授、两项研究的合著者玛拉·格哈 (Marla Geha) 表示：“在鲁宾天文台的数据中寻找新的银河系卫星对我职业生涯的大部分时间来说都是一个令人兴奋的未来前景。” “值得注意的是，这现在已成为现实。”

paras.en: The research involved a broad international collaboration. In addition to Yale, participating institutions included the University of Chicago, the University of Virginia, the University of Washington, Dartmouth College, the University of Tampa, NSF NOIRLab, Duke University, the University of Toronto, the Instituto de Astrofísica de Andalucía in Spain, the University of Colorado-Boulder, and Lund University in Sweden.
paras.zh: 该研究涉及广泛的国际合作。除耶鲁大学外，参与机构还包括芝加哥大学、弗吉尼亚大学、华盛顿大学、达特茅斯学院、坦帕大学、NSF NOIRLab、杜克大学、多伦多大学、西班牙安达卢西亚天文研究所、科罗拉多大学博尔德分校和瑞典隆德大学。

paras.en: Aashay Pai of the University of Chicago served as the first author of the study describing Rubin-GC1.
paras.zh: 芝加哥大学的 Aashay Pai 是该研究的第一作者，该研究描述了 Rubin-GC1。

paras.en: Hidden Galaxies Could Reveal New Clues About Dark Matter
paras.zh: 隐藏的星系可能揭示有关暗物质的新线索

paras.en: Finding additional satellites could do much more than expand the known population of galaxies surrounding the Milky Way. These faint objects may also help astronomers investigate one of the universe's greatest mysteries: dark matter.
paras.zh: 寻找更多的卫星不仅仅可以扩大银河系周围已知的星系数量。这些微弱的物体还可能帮助天文学家调查宇宙最大的谜团之一：暗物质。

paras.en: Dark matter is an invisible form of matter that does not emit or reflect light, making it impossible to observe directly with conventional telescopes. Scientists infer its existence from the gravitational effects it produces on stars, galaxies, and other cosmic structures. It accounts for most of the matter in the universe and provides much of the gravitational framework that holds galaxies together.
paras.zh: 暗物质是一种不可见的物质形式，不发射或反射光，因此无法用传统望远镜直接观察。科学家根据它对恒星、星系和其他宇宙结构产生的引力效应来推断它的存在。它解释了宇宙中的大部分物质，并提供了将星系聚集在一起的大部分引力框架。

paras.en: Ultra-faint galaxies such as Aquarius IV are particularly valuable for studying dark matter. They contain only a small fraction of the stars found in larger galaxies, yet dark matter dominates their total mass. By examining their properties and movements, researchers can test ideas about how dark matter behaves and influences the formation of galaxies.
paras.zh: 像水瓶座 IV 这样的超微弱星系对于研究暗物质特别有价值。它们只包含较大星系中发现的恒星的一小部分，但暗物质在它们的总质量中占主导地位。通过检查它们的性质和运动，研究人员可以测试有关暗物质如何行为和影响星系形成的想法。

paras.en: These discoveries could also help scientists reconstruct the Milky Way's long history. The positions, motions, and properties of small satellite galaxies can reveal how larger galaxies assembled over billions of years, including how they accumulated matter and interacted with smaller systems.
paras.zh: 这些发现还可以帮助科学家重建银河系的悠久历史。小卫星星系的位置、运动和特性可以揭示较大的星系在数十亿年的时间里如何聚集，包括它们如何积累物质并与较小的系统相互作用。

paras.en: Rubin's early findings may also provide important clues about how the universe's smallest and faintest galaxies form, evolve, and survive.
paras.zh: 鲁宾的早期发现也可能为宇宙中最小和最微弱的星系如何形成、演化和生存提供重要线索。

paras.en: "These discoveries are incredibly promising," Geha said. "Continued discoveries will allow us to complete the census of satellite galaxies around the Milky Way, which is a key to understanding how the faintest galaxies form."
paras.zh: “这些发现非常有希望，”格哈说。 “持续的发现将使我们能够完成对银河系周围卫星星系的普查，这是了解最微弱星系如何形成的关键。”

paras.en: Materials provided by Yale University. Original written by Jim Shelton. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

articles.title: What's that bright 'star' in the early morning sky? It's not a star at all!
articles.author: Joe Rao

paras.en: Early morning risers heading to work or school before sunrise are likely to notice a very bright, star-like object appearing low in the east-southeast sky just before sunrise. What is somewhat amazing is that just a couple of weeks ago this object wasn't there at all, but now it literally stands out with such brilliance as to almost command the attention of commuters who might be traveling in an easterly direction to "Look at me!"
paras.zh: 早起在日出前去上班或上学的人可能会注意到日出前在东南偏东的天空中出现了一个非常明亮的恒星状物体。令人惊奇的是，就在几周前，这个物体根本不存在，但现在它确实如此耀眼，几乎吸引了可能向东行驶的通勤者的注意力，让他们“看我！”

paras.en: The object in question is, of course, the planet Venus, which is currently amid one of its most spectacular forays into the morning sky, literally "vaulting up" into prominence.
paras.zh: 当然，所讨论的天体是金星，它目前正处于早晨天空中最壮观的一次尝试中，字面意思是“跃升”到显着位置。

paras.en: On Oct. 24, Venus came to inferior conjunction, passing between the Earth and sun and shifting from the evening into the morning sky. And the view is only going to get better in the days and weeks to come!
paras.zh: 10月24日，金星发生内合，穿过地球和太阳之间，从傍晚的天空转移到早晨的天空。在接下来的几天和几周内，景色只会变得更好！

paras.en: In terms of morning visibility, Venus is now in a literal and figurative sense "rising to the occasion." It's now rising before the break of dawn, more than 90 minutes before sunrise. From here on, it will rise three minutes earlier each day, so that by Dec. 17 it will rise 3 hours and 50 minutes before sunrise and blaze in a completely dark sky for more than two hours before the first vestige of morning twilight.
paras.zh: 就早晨的能见度而言，金星现在无论是字面意义上还是比喻意义上都“应势而生”。现在黎明前已经升起，距离日出还有 90 多分钟。从现在开始，它每天会提前三分钟升起，这样到12月17日，它将在日出前3小时50分钟升起，并在晨曦初现之前在完全黑暗的天空中闪耀两个多小时。

paras.en: It will reach peak brilliance on Nov. 29, when it will shine at an eye-popping magnitude of -4.9. That's 12 times brighter than its nearest planetary competitor, Jupiter and a full 25 times more dazzling than Sirius, the brightest of all stars. If you live in a rural location with no light pollution to interfere, you might be able to make out that it is casting a visible shadow and if you follow it right on through sunrise, it will be evident to your naked eye in full daylight: a tiny white speck plainly evident against the blue daytime sky.
paras.zh: 它将于 11 月 29 日达到峰值亮度，届时它将达到令人瞠目结舌的 -4.9 星等。它比最接近的行星竞争对手木星亮 12 倍，比所有恒星中最亮的天狼星亮 25 倍。如果你住在没有光污染干扰的乡村地区，你可能会发现它正在投下可见的阴影，如果你在日出时一直跟踪它，那么在白天，你的肉眼就会看到它：一个微小的白色斑点在蓝色的白天天空中清晰可见。

paras.en: In a way, we could even regard Venus as this year's version of a "Christmas Star," glowing with stunning radiance ". . . in the east" like the biblical quote mentioned in St. Matthew.
paras.zh: 在某种程度上，我们甚至可以将金星视为今年版本的“圣诞之星”，“……在东方”闪耀着令人惊叹的光芒，就像《马太福音》中提到的圣经引言一样。

paras.en: After reaching its high point in terms of morning visibility in mid-December, Venus will start a long, slow slide back toward the sun, rising about 1½ minutes later each morning from New Year's Day through late March. By then, Venus will be coming up as dawn is breaking, roughly 100 minutes before sunrise. Venus will continue to get gradually lower and rise progressively later during the spring and by late June it will be coming up less than an hour before sunrise, ultimately vanishing into the bright dawn twilight by July. Venus will then go on a "summer sabbatical" of sorts and will not reappear again until about this time next year when it will begin a very fine evening apparition.
paras.zh: 在 12 月中旬达到早晨能见度的最高点后，金星将开始漫长而缓慢地滑回太阳，从元旦到三月下旬，每天早上金星都会晚约 1.5 分钟升起。到那时，金星将在黎明时分升起，大约在日出前 100 分钟。金星将在春季继续逐渐降低并逐渐上升，到六月下旬，它将在日出前不到一个小时出现，最终在七月消失在明亮的黎明暮色中。然后金星将进行某种“夏季休假”，直到明年这个时候它才会再次出现，届时它将开始一个非常美好的夜晚显现。

paras.en: So, if any of your friends or relatives remark to you that they saw a "strange UFO" on the way to work or school recently, you now can set them straight.
paras.zh: 因此，如果您的任何朋友或亲戚对您说他们最近在上班或上学的路上看到了“奇怪的不明飞行物”，您现在可以纠正他们。

paras.en: Joe Rao serves as an instructor and guest lecturer at New York's Hayden Planetarium. He writes about astronomy for Natural History magazine, Sky and Telescope, The Old Farmer's Almanac and other publications.
paras.zh: Joe Rao 担任纽约海登天文馆的讲师和客座讲师。他为《自然历史》杂志、《天空与望远镜》、《老农年鉴》和其他出版物撰写有关天文学的文章。

paras.en: Joe Rao is Space.com's skywatching columnist, as well as a veteran meteorologist and eclipse chaser who also serves as an instructor and guest lecturer at New York's Hayden Planetarium. He writes about astronomy for Natural History magazine, Sky & Telescope and other publications. Joe is an 8-time Emmy-nominated meteorologist who served the Putnam Valley region of New York for over 21 years. You can find him on Twitter and YouTube tracking lunar and solar eclipses, meteor showers and more. To find out Joe's latest project, visit him on Twitter.
paras.zh: 乔·拉奥 (Joe Rao) 是 Space.com 的天空观察专栏作家，也是一位资深气象学家和日食追踪者，同时也是纽约海登天文馆的讲师和客座讲师。他为《自然历史》杂志、《天空与望远镜》和其他出版物撰写有关天文学的文章。 Joe 是一位曾 8 次获得艾美奖提名的气象学家，为纽约普特南谷地区服务超过 21 年。您可以在 Twitter 和 YouTube 上找到他跟踪月食、日食、流星雨等。要了解 Joe 的最新项目，请访问他的 Twitter。

articles.title: 'I think we will prevail': NASA chief Jared Isaacman on Artemis, China and the new moon race (exclusive)
articles.author: Chelsea Gohd

paras.en: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman is serious about launching "big rockets" to the moon every single year for the agency's Artemis program. And the new space race with China is fueling that ambition.
paras.zh: 美国宇航局局长贾里德·艾萨克曼认真考虑每年为该机构的阿尔忒弥斯计划向月球发射“大型火箭”。与中国的新太空竞赛正在助长这一雄心。

paras.en: "I feel good. I feel like we are certainly on a more achievable path to the lunar surface today than where we were before," Isaacman told Space.com.
paras.zh: “我感觉很好。我觉得今天我们肯定比以前更容易到达月球表面，”艾萨克曼告诉 Space.com。

paras.en: We recently sat down with the NASA chief to discuss the state of the Artemis program, and, off the bat, he made it clear that he's confident in the U.S. space program following the success of April's Artemis II mission around the moon. In fact, just prior to our conversation, it was announced that Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman will become the new deputy director of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. But the road from Artemis II's success to crewed lunar landings and, later, a permanent moon base will take a lot of launches of NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) megarocket, Isaacman stressed.
paras.zh: 我们最近与美国宇航局局长坐下来讨论阿尔忒弥斯计划的状况，他立即明确表示，继四月阿尔忒弥斯二号绕月任务取得成功后，他对美国的太空计划充满信心。事实上，就在我们谈话之前，有消息称阿耳忒弥斯二号指挥官里德·怀斯曼将成为美国宇航局喷气推进实验室的新副主任。但艾萨克曼强调，从阿耳忒弥斯二号的成功到载人登月以及后来的永久月球基地，将需要美国宇航局太空发射系统（SLS）巨型火箭进行多次发射。

paras.en: "You know, a lot of people, especially in the space community, start getting [into] if the landers are there or not. I don't really care about that right now. What I care about is that we are launching big rockets no less than once a year," he said.
paras.zh: “你知道，很多人，尤其是太空界的人，开始关注着陆器是否存在。我现在并不关心这个。我关心的是我们每年至少发射一次大型火箭，”他说。

paras.en: "I think that's imperative for NASA to be doing these deep-space human spaceflight missions right now," Isaacman added. "So, we had a great mission in April of '26. We will launch again in '27."
paras.zh: 艾萨克曼补充说：“我认为美国宇航局现在必须执行这些深空载人航天任务。” “所以，我们在 26 年 4 月肩负着一项伟大的使命。我们将在 27 年再次发射。”

paras.en: That coming launch will be for Artemis III, a crewed mission to low Earth orbit that will test docking procedures between NASA's Orion capsule and one or both of the Artemis program's private lunar landers — SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon.
paras.zh: 即将发射的阿耳忒弥斯 III 号是一项近地轨道载人任务，将测试 NASA 的猎户座太空舱与阿耳忒弥斯计划的一个或两个私人月球着陆器（SpaceX 的星舰和蓝色起源的蓝月亮）之间的对接程序。

paras.en: "We need to continue to exercise those muscles," he said, referring to SLS liftoffs. "And, honestly, once a year isn't great, either. I mean, I don't think we're going to get back to the early [space] shuttle days, you know, four missions a year. I don't think we're going to get back to where we were with Apollo, but once a year is the minimum … I would testify that to Congress in this role years down the road.
paras.zh: “我们需要继续锻炼这些肌肉，”他在谈到 SLS 升空时说道。 “而且，老实说，每年一次也不是很好。我的意思是，我不认为我们会回到早期的[太空]航天飞机时代，你知道，每年四次任务。我不认为我们会回到阿波罗计划的状态，但每年一次是最少的......我会在未来几年向国会证明这一点。

paras.en: "If NASA is going to be doing deep-space missions, complicated missions, [we should] launch at least once a year and get as much out of it as you can for taking the risk and spending the taxpayer dollars and building towards something greater," Isaacman added. "That's what we're doing with Artemis III, and that's what's going to better prepare us for Artemis IV."
paras.zh: 艾萨克曼补充道：“如果美国宇航局要执行深空任务、复杂的任务，我们应该每年至少发射一次，并尽可能多地利用它来承担风险，花纳税人的钱，朝着更伟大的目标迈进。” “这就是我们对阿耳忒弥斯三号所做的事情，这也是我们为阿耳忒弥斯四号做好更好准备的事情。”

paras.en: So, how is NASA coping with the challenges that face them as they approach Artemis III ahead of a crewed lunar landing on Artemis IV, which is targeted for 2028? While NASA can learn some lessons from past moon missions with Apollo, today it's primarily relying on the extensive experience and talent within the agency, according to Isaacman.
paras.zh: 那么，在计划于 2028 年载人登月阿耳忒弥斯四号之前，NASA 如何应对在接近阿耳忒弥斯三号时所面临的挑战呢？艾萨克曼表示，虽然美国宇航局可以从过去的阿波罗登月任务中吸取一些教训，但如今它主要依赖于该机构内部的丰富经验和人才。

paras.en: "Artemis II is very different from Apollo 8, and Artemis III will be very different from Apollo 9," he said. "Our approach is not exactly the same as it was … But what is the same right now? The spirit, the energy, the potential within NASA. The talent of the workforce and industry is no different than the 1960s."
paras.zh: “阿耳忒弥斯二号与阿波罗 8 号有很大不同，阿耳忒弥斯三号也将与阿波罗 9 号有很大不同，”他说。 “我们的方法与以前不完全相同……但现在有什么相同之处？NASA 内部的精神、活力和潜力。劳动力和行业的人才与 1960 年代没有什么不同。”

paras.en: There's another similarity to the Apollo era: NASA has a rival in its race to the moon. While the adversary in the 1960s was the Soviet Union, today the U.S. is competing against China.
paras.zh: 与阿波罗时代还有另一个相似之处：美国宇航局在登月竞赛中有一个竞争对手。 20世纪60年代的对手是苏联，而今天美国的对手是中国。

paras.en: "It is a real space race," Isaacman said. But, he added, "this one is very different than the first one."
paras.zh: “这是一场真正的太空竞赛，”艾萨克曼说。但是，他补充道，“这一次与第一个非常不同。”

paras.en: "Everything is closer than it was, not just in space. I mean, we had the edge in computing [and] every one of the technology domains during the Cold War. Our capabilities were better by a mile," he said. "[But with] China, it's not [like that]. They're very close."
paras.zh: “一切都比以前更近了，不仅仅是在太空。我的意思是，冷战期间我们在计算和每一个技术领域都拥有优势。我们的能力要好得多，”他说。 “[但对于]中国来说，情况并非如此。他们非常接近。”

paras.en: "We're saying we're going to land on the moon at the end of 2028. China is saying by the end of 2029," Isaacman added. "And it's like, Well, are they going to pull it off? Yes, they will. They've showcased their landers, their rovers, their suits, two-launch architecture with built-in reusability."
paras.zh: “我们说我们将在 2028 年底登陆月球。中国说是 2029 年底，”艾萨克曼补充道。 “这就像，好吧，他们会成功吗？是的，他们会的。他们展示了他们的着陆器、漫游车、宇航服、具有内置可重复使用性的两次发射架构。”

paras.en: So NASA is taking the Chinese threat very seriously, according to Isaacman.
paras.zh: 艾萨克曼表示，美国宇航局正在非常严肃地对待中国的威胁。

paras.en: "The consequence of getting this wrong, I'm telling you — it's going to be felt around the world," he said. "It will call everything into question."
paras.zh: “我告诉你，犯错的后果——全世界都会感受到，”他说。 “这会让一切都受到质疑。”

paras.en: "Should I be using American superintelligence or AI? Should I be doing Chinese? Should I be buying their computers? Should I be [buying] ours? Buying their cars, their airplanes, their ships? Whose security guarantees to trust?" Isaacman added. "I think the implications are pretty severe, which is why we're taking it so seriously and putting such extreme focus on the mission right now. But we have that playbook of success, and I think we will prevail."
paras.zh: “我应该使用美国的超级智能还是人工智能？我应该做中国的吗？我应该购买他们的计算机吗？我应该[购买]我们的吗？购买他们的汽车、飞机、轮船？谁的安全保证值得信任？”艾萨克曼补充道。 “我认为其影响相当严重，这就是为什么我们如此认真地对待它，并高度关注现在的使命。但我们有成功的剧本，我认为我们会取得胜利。”

paras.en: Chelsea Gohd served as a Senior Writer for Space.com from 2018 to 2022 before returning in 2026, covering everything from climate change to planetary science and human spaceflight in both articles and on-camera in videos. With a M.S. in Biology, Chelsea has written and worked for institutions including NASA JPL, the American Museum of Natural History, Scientific American, Discover Magazine Blog, Astronomy Magazine, and Live Science. When not writing, editing or filming something space-y, Gohd is writing music and performing as Foxanne, even launching a song to space in 2021 with Inspiration4. You can follow her online @chelsea.gohd and @foxanne.music
